The wording should be disaggregated.","BATCH-0051-E009 is used for gender-violence impunity even though its supplied question mapping does not include 6B.8. Its exact passage supports the factual claim, but the answer should explain this cross-question use rather than silently treating it as indexed evidence.","The answer describes IMSS-BIENESTAR complaint channels as evidence of “some institutional remedy.” The operating rules establish complaint intake, investigation, resolution, and notification requirements, but no cited passage demonstrates that complaints actually produced remedies in 2023."],"material_omissions":["The full index contains directly relevant evidence omitted from the answer: BATCH-0003-E021 reports cuts to women’s services and presidential hostility toward feminists; BATCH-0041-E003 reports weak or reduced 2023 funding for violence-against-women, shelter, and victim programs; BATCH-0015-E001/E003/E005-E008 document concrete migrant-child protection capacity, staffing, funding, procedural, and remedy failures.","The answer omits BATCH-0032-E007 and BATCH-0031-E018, which provide direct group-disaggregated poverty and deprivation figures for Indigenous people and people with disabilities and would substantiate the otherwise generic reference to opportunity gaps.","It omits BATCH-0006-E006, which directly tests whether femicide laws reduced violence and concludes that legal enactment was insufficient under impunity—highly pertinent to the enactment-versus-enforcement distinction.","It does not mention favorable practical evidence such as CNDH’s 371 complaints against officials and follow-up activity in BATCH-0021-R01-E010, even though this could qualify the conclusion about available remedies.","Accessibility is treated mainly through reading materials and compliance ratings; the index also contains education, health, emergency-service, shelter, and child-protection evidence that would give a fuller cross-domain assessment."]},{"question_id":"6B.9","factual_support_1_to_5":3,"completeness_1_to_5":2,"balance_1_to_5":4,"attribution_and_period_1_to_5":4,"judge_usefulness_1_to_5":3,"material_errors":["The claim that “integrated state health networks were not implemented as planned because of policy changes and a new health model” appears in the supplied fact summary for BATCH-0052-E017 but not in its exact cited excerpt. The excerpt provided begins with other Objective 3 indicators and does not contain that failed-network finding, so the material claim is not verifiable from the exact passage supplied.","The answer says the health system’s “institutional transition was associated with deteriorating access” and then combines 2018–2022 outcomes with the 2023 IMSS-BIENESTAR arrangement. The cited CONEVAL passages associate deterioration principally with the Seguro Popular-to-Insabi transition, pandemic effects, and coordination problems; they do not establish that the newly formalized 2023 IMSS-BIENESTAR rules caused those earlier outcomes.","“IMSS-BIENESTAR had statutory-administrative authority” is imprecise. The cited 2023 instrument establishes mandatory operating rules grounded in federal statutes and administrative authority, but the program’s annual rules are not themselves proof of durable statutory entrenchment beyond the fiscal year.","“Auditability” is supported, but the answer risks implying completed oversight. The exact rules say expenditures could be reviewed and prescribe evaluation and follow-up; they provide no completed 2023 audit findings or demonstrated corrective action.","The broad phrase “weakened autonomous oversight” is supported for IFT, COFECE, and the administration’s stance toward INAI, but those regulators are not themselves social-service institutions. Their relevance to the specific durability question should be explained rather than presented as direct evidence about the social-service system."],"material_omissions":["The answer omits extensive direct 2023 evidence about CONEVAL’s institutional performance: BATCH-0006-E003, BATCH-0013-E007/E008, and BATCH-0054-E007 report completed evaluations, dissemination, improvement commitments, information use, and stakeholder satisfaction. These are central to professional staffing, transparency, and institutionalized standards.","It omits BATCH-0054-E005/E006 and BATCH-0052-E002/E003/E005/E006/E008, which give the strongest systematic evidence on the design quality, coverage indicators, results orientation, component-purpose linkage, and budgets of the full priority-program portfolio in 2023.","It omits BATCH-0052-E001’s direct budget evidence: priority-program spending rose substantially overall while health-and-medicines spending fell 35% from 2020. This is essential for a differentiated assessment of funding reliability rather than a generalized statement about annual appropriations.","It omits BATCH-0015-E001/E005/E007/E008, which directly assess whether migrant-child institutions had adequate budgets, staffing, professional teams, procedures, data, and nationwide implementation—the precise elements asked by 6B.9.","It omits BATCH-0003-E005 and BATCH-0018-E017, which report closure of the National Human Identification Center and nonoperation of legally required forensic systems, strong evidence against continuity and durability.","It omits positive durable-institution evidence including the 2023 Annual Report on Poverty and Social Lag and FAIS reporting framework (BATCH-0012-E001/E003), the statutory CONEVAL framework and public technical materials, and formal program-monitoring systems beyond IMSS-BIENESTAR.","It omits BATCH-0038-E005 on Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro’s monthly evaluations, workplace verification, defined benefit, and reported reach, as well as BATCH-0049-E006 on the broader 2023 social-program budget.","It omits BATCH-0050-E004 and BATCH-0032-E006 on the scale, funding growth, and institutional continuity of the older-adult pension, which is one of the administration’s most consequential social institutions.","The answer does not separate institutions created or materially redesigned by AMLO from inherited institutions merely operating during his term. CONEVAL predates the administration, while IMSS-BIENESTAR combines an older program with a 2023 reorganization; this distinction is essential to the question’s verb “create.”","Post-rule resilience is correctly identified as unproven, but the index contains retrospective end-of-term evidence and 2024 continuation evidence that could at least test institutional survival after October 2024. The answer does not discuss why those candidates were excluded."]}],"verdict":"pass_with_corrections","strengths":["Both answers distinguish formal design from demonstrated enforcement or outcomes.","Both answers appropriately limit personal attribution and recognize the roles of Congress, courts, autonomous bodies, subnational authorities, agencies, and international partners.","The period limitations are explicit, especially for 2022 outcome data used as a baseline for 2023.","The answers present favorable and adverse evidence rather than equating legal enactment with practical success."],"systemic_problems":["Neither answer adequately covers the complete candidate index; several of the most directly responsive institutional, budgetary, staffing, implementation, and group-disaggregated candidates are omitted.","Some claims rely on fact summaries rather than propositions visible in the supplied exact excerpts.","Formal complaint, audit, evaluation, and supervision provisions are occasionally described too close to actual remedy or operational performance.","The 6B.9 answer does not consistently distinguish creation, continuation, reorganization, and inherited institutional capacity."],"concrete_corrections_required":["For 6B.8, disaggregate the detention findings by group and avoid implying that every group experienced the same form of discriminatory or arbitrary detention.","Describe IMSS-BIENESTAR complaint systems as prescribed mechanisms unless actual 2023 resolution outcomes are cited.","Add the omitted evidence on women’s-service funding, migrant-child implementation, disability and Indigenous deprivation, femicide-law effectiveness, and CNDH remedy activity.","For 6B.9, remove or replace the integrated-health-network claim unless the exact supporting passage is supplied.","Do not attribute 2018–2022 health-access deterioration to the 2023 IMSS-BIENESTAR arrangement; identify Seguro Popular-to-Insabi restructuring, pandemic effects, and coordination failures separately.","Add the 2023 CONEVAL performance and priority-program portfolio evidence, child-protection capacity evidence, forensic-institution closures or nonoperation, pension durability evidence, and direct budget trends.","Explicitly classify each institution as created, redesigned, inherited, or merely operated under López Obrador, and evaluate statutory authority, funding, staffing, transparency, and resilience separately.","Treat auditability, evaluations, complaints, and supervision as formal design unless completed audits, published results, resolved complaints, or corrective actions are documented."],"safe_for_judge_use":false,"rationale":"The answers are analytically cautious and mostly faithful to the cited passages, but they are not complete enough for skeptical judge use against the supplied full candidate index. Question 6B.9 has a material exact-passage verification failure and conflates pre-2023 health outcomes with the 2023 institutional transition. Both answers require targeted evidentiary additions and narrower wording before they can safely anchor a chapter judgment."}
